title: Hydrogen: the Lyman α line and the Balmer series
caption: With E_n = −13.6 eV/n², dropping from n = 3 to n = 2 releases 13.6(1/4 − 1/9) = 1.89 eV: λ = hc/ΔE = 656 nm, the red Hα line. Transitions ending on n = 2 give the visible Balmer lines (Hα 656, Hβ 486, Hγ 434, Hδ 410 nm); 2 → 1 (Lyman α, 122 nm) is ultraviolet.
alt: Hydrogen energy levels n = 1 to 6 with downward arrows for 2 to 1 at 122 nm in the ultraviolet and for 3, 4, 5 and 6 to 2 at 656, 486, 434 and 410 nm in the visible, with the line spectrum below.
description: Hydrogen's levels E_n = −13.6 eV/n² for n = 1 to 6 (the upper levels are spread out, not to scale).
The Balmer series: n = 3, 4, 5, 6 down to n = 2 gives 656, 486, 434 and 410 nm, all visible.
Lyman α (2 → 1) is 122 nm, in the ultraviolet.
